grammar.title: Future tenses
grammar.short: will, be going to, present simple and present continuous for the future

slides.sub: Planet Earth: plans to make a difference
slides.hook: What is your school going to do for the environment this year? What do you think the planet will be like in 2050?

slides.h: Four ways to talk about the future
rows: will + verb
Predictions (opinion), instant decisions, promises, offers
I think climate change will threaten more species. / I'll sign the petition!
be going to + verb
Plans and intentions; predictions with evidence
We're going to launch a campaign. / Look at the smoke! The forest is going to burn.
Present continuous
Fixed arrangements (time, place, people)
We're meeting our sponsors on Friday.
Present simple
Timetables and schedules
The climate march starts at 10 a.m.

p: Use 'will' when you decide something at the moment of speaking, for promises and offers, and for predictions based on opinion (I think, probably, I'm sure).
ex: You need volunteers? I**'ll give** my time on Saturday!
I promise I **won't use** plastic bags any more.
I think green energy **will be** cheaper in the future.

p: Use 'be going to' for plans you've already decided, and for predictions based on what you can see now.
ex: Our eco club **is going to raise** funds for the animal shelter.
We**'re going to reduce** our carbon footprint: no more car to school!
Look at the river! The factory **is going to damage** the habitat.

p: Present continuous: arrangements already organized (in your diary).
ex: We**'re holding** a fundraising event on Saturday.
The bus to the nature reserve **leaves** at 8:15 tomorrow.

slides.title: Save the river!
text: Marta: Big news! We**'re meeting** the mayor on Monday at 5. 🙌
Dani: Amazing. What **are** we **going to ask** for?
Marta: We**'re going to launch** a campaign to protect the river habitat. Many species are suffering.
Dani: I**'ll make** the posters! I think lots of people **will sign** the petition.
Marta: Perfect. The meeting **finishes** at 6, so we can hold an event after.

items: You need help? OK, I'm going to help you!
You need help? OK, I'll help you!
Decision at the moment of speaking → will.
I will meet the sponsors at 6. It's in my diary.
When we will reach our target, we'll celebrate.
When we reach our target, we'll celebrate.
After when / as soon as / before, use the present simple.

grammar.title: Future continuous
grammar.short: Actions in progress at a time in the future

slides.sub: Planet Earth: where will you be in 2050?
slides.hook: What will you be doing this time next year? Will people be living in sustainable cities in 2050?

rows: will be + verb-ing
We will be using only green energy.
won't be + verb-ing
We won't be driving petrol cars.
Will + subject + be + verb-ing?
Will you be volunteering at the beach clean-up?

slides.h: Use 1: in progress at a future time
p: We use the future continuous for an action that will be happening at a particular moment in the future.
ex: At 10 a.m. tomorrow, we**'ll be marching** to save the planet.
This time next week I**'ll be planting** trees with the eco club.
In 2050, people **will be living** in green, sustainable cities.

p: It's a polite way to ask about someone's plans, especially before asking for a favour.
ex: **Will** you **be using** your bike tomorrow? I want to reduce my carbon footprint!
**Will** you **be coming** to the fundraising event?

rows: The event will start at 5. (a moment)
At 5:30 we'll be raising funds. (in progress)
I'll donate money tonight.
Don't call at 8 – I'll be signing petitions online.

slides.title: Dear me in 2050
text: Dear future me, I hope you **will be living** in a city with clean air. I imagine that most people **will be cycling** to work and that factories **won't be producing** so much greenhouse gas.
Maybe you **will be working** as a scientist, helping endangered species to survive. Maybe you **will be teaching** children how to protect their habitat.
Whatever you **are doing**, I hope you are still making a difference!

items: This time tomorrow I will signing petitions.
This time tomorrow I will be signing petitions.
At 9 p.m. I'll be knowing if we reached our target.
At 9 p.m. I'll know if we reached our target.
State verbs don't usually use continuous forms.
